title: Codec-aware payload benchmark briefing
content:
Purpose
This is a working brief that explores how request payload encoding (JSON, gzipped JSON, protobuf/msgpack, and streaming chunked payloads) affects observed end-to-end latency and per-request cost on Redwood inference stacks. The goal is to surface actionable guidance for SDK/Console recommendations and a small set of code-path optimizations we can ship in the console and SDKs.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Payload serialization and HTTP transfer time can be a non-trivial fraction of p50/p95 for short prompts (< 200 tokens).
- gzipped-json reduces network time dramatically for large text inputs (> 5 KB) but introduces CPU overhead on client and server sides; net win for hosted but mixed for low-power edge nodes.
- Binary encodings (protobuf/msgpack) reduce bytes and serialization time vs text JSON in our microbenchmarks and are consistently helpful for high QPS flows.
- Streaming chunked uploads reduce p95 for very large contexts (long context windows) by overlapping transfer and tokenization, but complicate retries and observability.

Experiment setup (notes)
- Conducted on: Dedicated pool (A100-80GB, 4x GPUs), Hosted API fronted by edge proxies in us-west1, client box simulating 1Gbps connection.
- Runtime build: runtime@main (commit: a7f3c4b), server side recv/deserialize single-threaded unless otherwise specified.
- Payload types tested: small prompt (0.5 KB), medium (6 KB), large (80 KB), multimodal (image base64 in JSON ~1MB).
- Measurements: p50, p95, p99 of end-to-end request time (client send to first token emitted), server CPU% during deserialize, bytes on the wire, and observed per-request billing delta (approx) based on tokenization + byte-transport heuristics used in billing pipeline.

Baseline numbers (representative)
- Small prompt (0.5 KB):
  - JSON: p50 18ms, p95 48ms, p99 110ms; bytes=600 B
  - msgpack: p50 15ms, p95 40ms, p99 90ms; bytes=520 B
  - gzipped JSON: p50 22ms (serialize gz), p95 52ms, p99 115ms; bytes=300 B
- Medium prompt (6 KB):
  - JSON: p50 60ms, p95 240ms, p99 420ms; bytes=6.6 KB
  - msgpack: p50 47ms, p95 200ms, p99 380ms; bytes=5.8 KB
  - gzipped JSON: p50 38ms, p95 120ms, p99 260ms; bytes=1.2 KB
- Large prompt (80 KB):
  - JSON: p50 420ms, p95 1850ms, p99 3200ms; bytes=81 KB
  - gzipped JSON: p50 120ms, p95 420ms, p99 950ms; bytes=9 KB (gzip ratio ~9x)
  - streaming (chunked): p50 140ms, p95 360ms, p99 800ms (overlap wins on first-token latency vs full upload)

ASCII charts (throughput/latency shape simplified)
- Medium prompt p95 by encoding:
  JSON     |█████████████████████████ 240ms
  msgpack  |██████████████████ 200ms
  gzip     |██████████ 120ms

- Bytes on wire (large prompt):
  JSON     : [#################################] 81 KB
  gzip     : [#####] 9 KB

Observations and interpretation
1) Small prompts
   - Absolute numbers dominated by network RTT and server queuing. Serialization choice matters less for p50 but can shift p99 when client serialization blocks the worker thread (e.g., heavy JSON construction in slow languages).
   - Actionable: prefer binary encoding only for high-QPS SDKs; but default JSON is ergonomically fine for interactive dev flows.

2) Medium/large prompts
   - gzip wins materially on network-bound stacks. When server decompression is single-threaded and contends with inference CPU, the CPU overhead can increase p99 under high concurrency.
   - msgpack/protobuf provide a balanced sweet spot: smaller bytes than JSON with lower CPU overhead than gzip.

3) Streaming
   - For very long contexts (multi-document, embeddings + context), chunked uploads reduce first-token latency by ~30-60% versus waiting for full payload. But complexity: partial tokenization, missing chunk handling, and increased tracing complexity.

4) Multimodal payloads (base64 images in JSON)
   - Base64 inflates bytes by ~33%. If clients can send binary (multipart or protobuf with raw bytes), p95 and cost both improve. Recommend SDK helper to detect and convert base64 to multipart.

Cost implications (notes)
- Billing interplay: tokenization cost scales with tokenized input; network egress charge negligible in hosted cluster for internal traffic but API gateway egress for large multimodal payloads adds cost for customer.
- Example: large 80KB JSON -> gzipping reduces billable transport bytes (internal charge) and reduces client-side wait; but server decompress CPU contributes to resource contention which can increase effective compute cost per request during spikes.

Recommendations (short list)
- Console/UI: Add an encoding hint and size advisory when users paste large contexts. Default suggestion: use gzipped JSON for > 8 KB when using hosted API; show tradeoffs (CPU vs network).
- SDK: Add opt-in binary-encoding mode (msgpack) and transparent multipart for raw binary attachments (images) to avoid base64 bloat. Provide a toggle to enable client-side gzip for large payloads with automatic backoff if server signals high CPU.
- Server: Add decompression worker pool (off-main-thread) and async deserialize path to reduce p99 amplification under concurrency. Mark as internal perf ticket.
- Streaming: Prototype chunked upload + early-tokenization in a feature branch; add e2e tests and retry semantics.

Open questions / TODOs
- Need to measure effect on Dedicated T4/Tesla style nodes (lower decompression throughput) — likely gzip less attractive there.
- Add production tracing hook to surface per-request serialization time in Console (split client-serialize, network, server-deserialize).
- Investigate zero-copy deserialization libs in our server language (C++/Rust shim) to reduce JSON parse CPU.

Appendix: quick action tickets
- GH PR: runtime: introduce async-decompress worker pool; draft PR linked above. (owner: Jun)
- SDK: add msgpack mode + multipart helper; implement in node/py SDKs. (owner: Ethan)
- Console: size advisory UI + encoding toggle. (owner: Marta)

Notes to reviewer
- This is intentionally rough; numbers are median of several runs and will fluctuate with network conditions and cluster load. Use this as a directional brief for product/SDK prioritization.
- I left raw CSV outputs in the linked artifacts; will attach cleaned charts next iteration.

Scratch/side-notes
- Observed surprising p99 spikes on gzipped large prompts when concurrent decompress threads = 2 (server), likely GC/alloc churn in the language runtime. Add language-level profiling.
- Consider a hybrid: msgpack for structured metadata + gzip for large free-text blocks (best compression with moderate CPU).

End of brief.
